findings.reason: the honest change is a new source in gather_sources feeding the existing document rather than a parallel dialect read; the cadence and the coordinator-burn measurement §5 wants are exactly what the timer the plan calls missing already provides.
findings.text: §1 records the preflight surface as carrying the whole shape a heartbeat needs and missing only an input, but `paid_lanes` already IS that heartbeat for metered accounts: one document per account, republished by its own systemd timer every five minutes, reconciling each window by recency and carrying utilisation, reset, burn, projected exhaustion, source and observed-at, with staleness marked per window. The plan instead landed a parallel account reader (`Dialect.read_account_surface` + `probe_budget`, wired into the pre-flight at reckon/budget.py:813) alongside the existing document path the pre-flight already reads at reckon/budget.py:1456, and never added the fresh account-surface read as a source in `paid_lanes.gather_sources`. Two account-position paths can now disagree inside one pre-flight, which is the plan's own §5b defect (an unstated denominator) arriving as an unstated source.

findings.reason: §7 should cite the measured-boundary owner and say how endpoint-advertised `context_length` differs from a recorded refusal, or extend it; otherwise the section proposes as open a guard that is already half-built and unconnected to it.
findings.text: §7 leaves open whether reckon should verify a declared window against the endpoint it dispatches into, and its sidecar even notes effective_input_window "is partly built but not shown to fire", yet §7 never names it or its owner. `context_budget.refusal_census` already computes the lowest input the endpoint was observed refusing per lane, `_flight_schema.py:307` persists it as `effective_input_window`, and `_context_fit_verdict` (reckon/crew/routing.py:3212) already gates on min(declared, effective) so a lane whose endpoint enforces less than it declares is refused.

findings.reason: naming window_reading would force the plan to reconcile two readers of one quantity — stream-sourced versus account-sourced — which is the composition the plan needs to state.
findings.text: the prior-art reuse map (comment c-run-r-20260914T125344512535) was delivered and did locate the probe/transport seam, but the plan's citations stop at _backends/budget/dispatch and omit `reckon/crew/window_reading.py`, which already reads a stream's newest metered window (five_hour/seven_day, utilisation, reset, observation age) and states in its own docstring that it "deliberately" does not consult the account surface because that read fails. A plan adding an account-surface transport for the same metered-window quantity should say why the existing stream reader is not the reading, and the omission is what let the paid-lanes duplicate above go unseen.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the dialect's budget surface is spread across three entry points (budget_probe / read_probe / read_account_surface) with probe_budget choosing among them, instead of one interface a caller can hold as the one place a headroom figure comes from.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §1/§2 add a second metered-account reader beside the paid-lanes document, and §7 re-derives a boundary that effective_input_window/refusal_census already own.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's reuse map covers the _backends/budget/dispatch/probe seams but never cites reckon/crew/paid_lanes.py, the module that already publishes one document per metered account refreshed on its own clock, nor reckon/crew/window_reading.py.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §3 gives the justification the item asks for: the existing probe exchange is a request written to a held-open stdin, which cannot express an HTTPS read, so the dialect owning its own transport is a deepening rather than a passthrough.
